bug_description.normalized: The fuzzer copies attacker bytes into a fixed global buffer and feeds them to lwan's config lexer. In the staged PoC, byte offsets 796-801 are `''''''`: `lex_multiline_string()` treats 796-798 as the opener, `advance_n()` moves `lexer->start` to byte 799, and the immediate 799-801 closer makes `emit()` produce an empty `LEXEME_STRING` whose pointer still aliases the raw fuzz buffer. `parse_config()` buffers that empty token as a section-shorthand name, and `parse_section()` later calls `lwan_strbuf_append_str(..., lexeme->value.value, lexeme->value.len)` without rejecting `lexeme->value.len == 0`. In `lwan_strbuf_append_str()`, `sz == 0` means "treat `s2` as NUL-terminated" and triggers `strlen(s2)`. Because the lexeme pointer is just a span inside the copied fuzz data rather than a terminated C string, `strlen` reads through the end of `static_data` and AddressSanitizer reports a global-buffer-overflow read.

source.description: An empty multiline-string token is materialized from the attacker-controlled config buffer.
source.value_from: The harness copies the PoC into `static_data`. In the staged testcase, byte offsets 796-801 are six consecutive single quotes: 796-798 are the multiline-string opener and 799-801 are the immediate closer. `lex_config()` enters `lex_multiline_string()` at that opener, `advance_n()` moves `lexer->start` to offset 799, and `emit()` therefore creates a `LEXEME_STRING` with `.value = static_data + 799` and `.len = 0`.
source.note: This is the first scored project-side materialization of the vulnerability-relevant value: an empty string lexeme whose pointer still aliases the raw fuzz buffer. The resulting `.value == static_data + 799` is the source pointer consistent with the saved `strlen` read running to the end of the 32768-byte buffer.

root_cause.description: parse_section forwards a zero-length section-name lexeme to lwan_strbuf_append_str instead of rejecting an empty section name.
root_cause.note: The fix adds `if (!lexeme->value.len) { ... return NULL; }` immediately before this call. In the vulnerable code, `lexeme->value.len == 0` reaches `lwan_strbuf_append_str()` unchanged, which activates that helper's `strlen()` path on a non-NUL-terminated pointer.

sink.description: strlen() scans past the end of the global fuzz buffer because `s2` is a raw lexeme pointer, not a terminated C string.
sink.note: ASan reports `READ of size 31970` in `strlen`, reached from `lwan_strbuf_append_str` line 170, and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of global variable `static_data` in `src/bin/fuzz/config_fuzzer.cc`. Together with the 32768-byte `static_data` extent, that saved span is consistent with `s2` starting at `static_data + 799`.

parser_admitted.description: A newline after buffered string tokens routes the parser into the section-shorthand path.
parser_admitted.note: This is the control point that admits the empty buffered token into section parsing even though no explicit `{` was seen.

tainted_value_origin.description: The harness copies the attacker-controlled testcase bytes into the fixed global buffer that the config parser later lexes.
tainted_value_origin.note: After the copy, line 53 passes `static_data` and `size` to `config_open_for_fuzzing()`. No terminating NUL is appended, so later lexeme pointers alias raw bytes inside the same global array that ASan names in the crash report.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness copies the PoC into the fixed global `static_data` array and opens the config parser over that raw byte span.
The quote run at PoC offsets 796-801 (`''''''`) produces an empty `LEXEME_STRING`, and `parse_config()` buffers that zero-length token as a pending section-shorthand name.

When a newline arrives with buffered tokens, the parser takes the section-shorthand path, consumes the empty lexeme as the section name, and passes its pointer with `len == 0` to `lwan_strbuf_append_str()`.
Because `sz == 0`, `lwan_strbuf_append_str()` calls `strlen(s2)` on the raw lexeme pointer, and the read runs off the end of `static_data`, triggering the ASan global-buffer-overflow.

fine_trace.note: At PoC offsets 796-801 the input has `''''''`. `lex_config()` enters `lex_multiline_string()` on bytes 796-798, `advance_n()` at line 342 moves `lexer->start` to byte 799, and the immediate closing delimiter at 799-801 makes `emit()` build a `LEXEME_STRING` with `.value = static_data + 799` and `.len = 0`. That start offset matches the saved `strlen` span that ran from this lexeme pointer to the end of the 32768-byte fuzz buffer.
The zero-length `LEXEME_STRING` from step 1 is admitted into the parser's pending-token buffer, where it becomes the next section-shorthand name candidate.
When the lexer later emits a newline, this branch sees the buffered string token from step 2 and selects the section-shorthand parser instead of discarding the line.
parse_section consumes the first buffered token as the section name. The recovered `lexeme` still points into `static_data`, and its `value.len` is still 0.

Root cause. The vulnerable code does not reject `lexeme->value.len == 0` before forwarding the section name to `lwan_strbuf_append_str()`. The patch adds that missing empty-section guard immediately before this call.
The helper interprets a size of 0 as "compute the string length yourself." Because step 5 passed `lexeme->value.len == 0`, this branch is taken and execution falls into the `strlen(s2)` path.

Sink. `s2` is the attacker-controlled lexeme pointer from step 5, which aliases raw bytes inside `static_data` at offset 799 rather than a terminated C string. `strlen` therefore keeps reading until it crosses the end of the 32768-byte global buffer, producing the observed `READ of size 31970` and the ASan report at the right edge of `static_data`.

poc.trigger: In the saved PoC, offsets 796-801 form an empty multiline-string token (`''''''`) on a line that the parser treats as section shorthand. That makes the first buffered section-name lexeme empty, so `parse_section()` forwards its pointer with `len == 0` to `lwan_strbuf_append_str()`, which calls `strlen()` on the raw fuzz-buffer pointer and reads past `static_data`.
